title: Lakemont Bank - Data Residency & Compliance Discovery
summary: First discovery call to understand Lakemont Bank's data residency and compliance constraints. Key concerns: EU data residency for EU customers, strict logging controls for PCI/HIPAA-adjacent workflows, KMS integration and auditability, and need for Private or Dedicated deployment evaluation. Agreed next steps: send SOC2 and security whitepaper, schedule technical deep dive with SE to scope Private on-prem / VPC options, and propose pilot timeline.
next_steps: Alex Navarro: Send SOC2 report, security whitepaper, and compliance matrix (due: 2027-01-03)
Priya Shah: Schedule SE-led technical deep dive to demo Private deployment options and run initial benchmark (due: 2027-01-07)
Maria Alvarez: Share current network diagram and list of required IPs/VPC peering constraints (due: 2027-01-04)
Ethan Wright: Confirm list of data types considered PCI/HIPAA and any internal retention limits (due: 2027-01-05)
Alex Navarro: Provide pricing guidance for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private pilot (due: 2027-01-06)
action_items: Alex Navarro: Email SOC2 attestation + security whitepaper (due 2027-01-03)
Priya Shah: Prepare Private deployment checklist and high-level architecture options (due 2027-01-07)
Maria Alvarez: Upload VPC peering details and compliance contacts to shared drive (due 2027-01-04)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-27 15:00 EST | Duration: ~46m | Attendees: Alex Navarro, Priya Shah (Redwood)

John Peterson, Maria Alvarez, Ethan Wright (Lakemont Bank)

00:00 Alex Navarro: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, excited to talk through Lakemont's residency and compliance needs

can you hear me okay?

00:06 John Peterson: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks for the invite. We scheduled this to understand options


hosted, dedicated, private


and what fits our regulatory needs.

00:18 Priya Shah: Great, quick intro

I'm Priya, Redwood SE, I'll dive into the technical bits. Alex will handle commercial and high level. Could you run through your current deployment and constraints?

00:28 Maria Alvarez: Sure. We're a regional bank with EU customers and US customers. For EU customer data we have to ensure data stays in EU. We also have some customers with HIPAA-like requirements and PCI-scope systems, so logging and retention are sensitive. Right now we're on AWS with strict VPC controls.

00:45 Ethan Wright: To add, our compliance team is strict about any third-party logging. We can't send raw transcripts or PII to uncontrolled logging endpoints; auditability is required, with HSM-backed KMS for keys.

01:02 Alex Navarro: Understood. So primary constraints: region residency (EU), strict logging/audit controls, and KMS/HSM. We work across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private


quick definitions: Hosted is Redwood's managed service, Dedicated is reserved capacity with tenant isolation, Private is VPC or on-prem where control plane is private. We can map options to your needs.

01:20 John Peterson: Quick question

do you support EU-only data residency? We need to be sure that customer messages never leave EU data centers and logs are retained per our policy.

01:30 Priya Shah: For Hosted we have region controls


you can pin workloads to specific regions. There's also an option to restrict backups and logs to that region; that said, Hosted still has Redwood control plane access. For the strictest compliance we usually recommend Dedicated with VPC peering or Private deployment.
01:50 Maria Alvarez: So Dedicated gives us GPU pools isolated to our account but still managed by Redwood infra; what's the difference vs Private on network controls?

02:05 Priya Shah: Dedicated: you get dedicated GPU capacity and tenant isolation, and we can implement VPC peering or private endpoints. Private: the control plane itself can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem so you retain more control


workflows.
02:22 Ethan Wright: For KMS, can Redwood integrate with our AWS KMS or a customer HSM? We need keys to be customer-managed for at-rest encryption and for encrypting logs.

02:33 Alex Navarro: Yes, we support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we can do envelope encryption with customer KMS in some setups, but Private gives the clearest model where keys never leave your environment.

02:50 John Peterson: Logging

what are typical retention and access controls? We want to avoid PII in logs, and we need audit logs that show who accessed what model and prompts, ideally immutable.

03:02 Priya Shah: We have configurable logging levels: minimal (no user payloads), metadata-only, or full. For regulated workloads we recommend metadata-only plus explicit masking and prefix caching so user content doesn't get persisted. Audit logs can be sent to your SIEM via secure endpoint. Note: some auto-logs are generated by the control plane unless you choose Private/ Dedicated configurations that route logs to your endpoints.

03:28 Maria Alvarez: When you say masking

is there a built-in PII redaction or do we need to handle client-side?

03:35 Priya Shah: We have basic redaction helpers, but for deterministic compliance we recommend client-side redaction or proxying through a filter before sending. We also support per-route policies so certain endpoints never log prompt content.

03:49 Alex Navarro: Also worth calling out prefix/KV-cache: it's server-side optimization but we can disable it for sensitive data or ensure keys are customer-managed so nothing persists beyond SLO windows.

04:02 Ethan Wright: Regarding GDPR

how does Redwood handle deletion?

04:09 Priya Shah: On Private you control the data life cycle; you can run deletion scripts against persisted objects. On Dedicated we provide APIs to delete customer artifacts and purge cached KV state. Hosted has deletion flows but you need to coordinate and we retain some metadata for billing/audit per contract; we can include contractual terms for deletion timelines in the agreement.
04:28 John Peterson: Ok. We need to see the legal side on deletion timelines. Also, any certifications? SOC two? ISO 27001?

04:36 Alex Navarro: We have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001

I'll share the attestation and our security whitepaper post-call. For Private deployments you also inherit a lot of your own controls, but we provide audit logs to demonstrate Redwood-side activity.

04:52 Maria Alvarez: Are there known limitations for on-prem deployments

like specific GPU types or OS/driver compat?

05:00 Priya Shah: The on-prem package supports mainstream NVIDIA GPUs (A10, A100) and we've documented driver/kernel requirements. We'll share the hardware compatibility matrix. We also offer a lightweight private appliance for smaller groups but for full performance we recommend validated hardware.

05:18 John Peterson: Network egress

our procurement requires that no customer data is sent to third-party telemetry or analytics. How do you ensure that?

05:27 Alex Navarro: For Private/Dedicated we can disable third-party telemetry and we provide config flags that prevent outbound telemetry. For Hosted, we can limit telemetry, but some telemetry for platform health may still be optional


again, contractual addendum possible.
05:42 Ethan Wright: Auditability: We need an immutable audit trail for admin actions. Does Redwood support write-once logs or integration with our SIEM like Splunk/Datadog?

05:53 Priya Shah: Yes, we can stream audit logs to your SIEM via secure endpoint. We also support signing of audit events so you can validate immutability. For the strongest guarantees customers use Private with logs retained in their own storage with WORM policies.
06:10 Maria Alvarez: If we choose Dedicated and later move to Private, how painful is migration?

06:18 Priya Shah: We designed export paths for model configs, prompts, and policy rules. Data residency artifacts like logs need separate handover but it's a supported process


well collaborate on migration runbooks.
06:28 John Peterson: One of our bank's internal policies says vendor personnel should not have direct access to production prompts or PII. Can you support that?

06:36 Alex Navarro: Absolutely

Private gives you the strictest control. On Dedicated we can restrict Redwood console access and integrate your SSO and RBAC; we can also disable developer-level access by default and provide escalation workflows.
06:50 Ethan Wright: Any experience with HIPAA specifically? We have a couple of healthcare adjacent clients and want the option to handle PHI carefully.

06:58 Priya Shah: We have a HIPAA compliance pack and BAAs available for Dedicated and Private customers. Hosted can be supported under a BAA with certain controls


were route that to legal to confirm specifics.

07:12 Maria Alvarez: Pricing delta

ballpark how much more is Dedicated vs Hosted and then Private? Our procurement needs ranges to plan budgets.

07:20 Alex Navarro: Ballpark: Hosted is usage-based (tokens/embeddings). Dedicated is a reserved capacity model with monthly commit


typically higher base but lower per-token. Private includes license + deployment/ops costs. I'll follow up with a pricing sheet and example TCO comparisons tailored to your traffic profile.

07:36 John Peterson: For the technical deep dive, we'd like to run a short benchmark with representative workloads


latency and cost per 1k tokens, and verify that EU-residency holds under load.

07:48 Priya Shah: Sounds good. For benchmarking we'll need sample prompts and a test account. We can run on Dedicated capacity pinned to EU region or on Private if you want full control. Which do you prefer initially?
07:58 Maria Alvarez: Let's start with Dedicated in EU region for speed of setup, with a path to Private if the security team requires it.

08:06 Ethan Wright: One more question on logging restrictions

can you provide a schema of what gets logged (headers, prompt length, token counts, prompt content) so we can map to PCI/HIPAA requirements?

08:17 Priya Shah: Yes, we'll share a logging schema. By default we log metadata like request_id, model, route, token counts, latency; prompt content is opt-in. We'll include sample payloads in the doc.
08:30 Alex Navarro: I'll attach SOC2, the logging schema, and a sample Dedicated configuration for EU. Also I'll include the compliance contact for Redwood legal.

08:40 John Peterson: Timing

procurement tends to take 8-12 weeks for contracts like this. Our priority is to prove technical fit before procurement ramps up.

08:50 Alex Navarro: Understood. Proposed timeline: quick SE deep dive in 1-2 weeks, pilot (2-4 weeks), then procurement. We'll aim for the SE deep dive next Wednesday


is that feasible?
09:02 Maria Alvarez: Next Wednesday works. I'll invite our network engineer and procurement lead to the deep dive.

09:08 Priya Shah: Great, I'll prepare a tech agenda

architecture options (Dedicated EU pinned), KMS integration, logging flow, and a short benchmark plan.

09:18 Ethan Wright: Minor nit: you mentioned KV cache earlier

just ensure caches aren't storing raw PHI. We want an option to disable caches for specific routes.

09:28 Priya Shah: Absolutely

per-route cache disable and TTL controls are supported. We'll document the exact flags.
09:36 John Peterson: Any blockers we should know of?

09:39 Alex Navarro: None from our side. Main items are internal approvals, hardware validation if you choose on-prem, and agreeing on logging/retention SLAs. We'll send draft language for the DPA and BAA.
09:52 Maria Alvarez: Good. Can you also include sample contract clauses for data residency and deletion timelines? Legal will want drafts to start their review.
09:59 Alex Navarro: Yes, we'll send sample DPA clauses and data deletion timelines in the package.
10:06 Ethan Wright: Excellent. Anything else?
10:09 John Peterson: No, thanks. Looking forward to the deep dive.
10:12 Alex Navarro: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs. Talk soon.

10:16


meeting end
